properties.statement:
EVERY DESCRIPTION AROUND `Constraint` SAYS 'NUMERIC BUDGET' WHILE THE SCHEMA REQUIRES ONLY `name` AND `statement`, AND A CAREFUL READER THEREFORE RULED OUT THE EXACT NODE TYPE THEY NEEDED. Measured 2026-08-15 on a genesis session modelling the US federal government (docs/feedback/2026-08-15-usgov-genesis-session.md, item 3, which its own author graded the report's only HIGH severity).

WHAT THE SESSION CONCLUDED: that reflow2 has no home for a requirement that FORBIDS. It listed eleven constitutional prohibitions — no bill of attainder, no ex post facto law, no title of nobility, habeas corpus may not be suspended, Speech or Debate immunity, the Tenth Amendment reservation — and reasoned that `Constraint` 'requires quantity / limit / direction. Numeric budgets only. \"No ex post facto law\" has no unit.' It left all eleven as Requirements, knowing they would be reported unsatisfied forever, and deliberately did not silence them.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: `describe_schema {node_type: Constraint, required_only: true}` returns `name` and `statement`. NOTHING ELSE. `add_constraint`'s required list is `id`, `name`, `statement`; `quantity`, `limit`, `direction`, `category` and `objective` all carry `default: null`. AND THE TYPE'S OWN HINT IS THE USE CASE VERBATIM: 'A limit or rule the design MUST respect (vs. a Requirement, which is a goal to achieve). \"Must run offline\", \"budget under $5k\", \"no PII leaves the device\".' — 'no PII leaves the device' and 'no bill of attainder shall be passed' are the same sentence shape: a non-numeric prohibition, imposed rather than chosen, binding everything, owned by nobody. Constraint is the home for all eleven, with no schema change and no new node type, and CONSTRAINS reaches any node.

WHY THE READER WAS MISLED, WHICH IS THE DEFECT: the prose disagrees with the schema in one direction only. The served instructions say 'When the user states a NUMERIC LIMIT — a mass budget, an end-to-end latency, a cost cap — record it as a Constraint: add_constraint with quantity (unit-bearing), limit and direction.' `add_constraint`'s own description opens 'For a numeric budget (BL-11) set quantity...'. The kpp-proposal skill is entirely about thresholds and numbers. Three surfaces, all narrower than the type, none of them wrong sentence-by-sentence, and together they describe a budget primitive. The one place that states the truth is `describe_schema`, which the session did not call for this type and had no reason to: it was not guessing at an unusual node, it was reading the documentation for a familiar one.

⭐ SAME ROOT CAUSE AS `fact:defect-typed-tool-parameter-names-are-inconsistent`, AND THIS IS WHAT MAKES IT WORTH MORE THAN A DOC FIX. That fact records the helper layer disagreeing with the schema about FIELD NAMES — nine instances, each costing a failed call and a retry, correctly graded as individually trivial. This is the same disagreement about a node type's SCOPE, and the cost is not a retry: it is a modelling decision. The session graded the field-name instance it hit as 'low, but it costs a full round trip' and this one as 'high... a modelling-vocabulary gap, not a bug'. BOTH JUDGEMENTS ARE THE SAME DEFECT SEEN AT TWO PRICES, and the expensive one was invisible as a defect because it never produced an error — it produced a confident wrong conclusion and eleven permanently-open gaps.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the schema requires two fields; three documentation surfaces describe a numeric budget; one experienced reader concluded the type was unusable and modelled around it. WHAT IS NOT: how many other designs have made the same substitution (this is one observation), and whether the eleven were ever re-modelled — that is the other project's call, not reflow2's.

FIX SHAPES, smallest first: give `add_constraint`'s description a leading sentence for the non-numeric case before the budget paragraph; correct the served instructions' 'When the user states a numeric limit' to name prohibitions too; or, if the budget reading is the intended one, say so and answer where a non-numeric imposed limit belongs — but the hint already answers that, so the prose is what is wrong.
